source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A garment worker has numbness of the thumb, index and middle fingers. Holding the wrist flexed for a minute brings on tingling. This is:
questions.rationale: CTS is median nerve compression from repetitive hand work; Phalen's (wrist flexion) and Tinel's (tapping) signs are positive.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Carpal tunnel syndrome (PDF p. 413)
questions.quote: (+) Phalen's sign (tingling sensation on holding the WTist in flexion for few minutes).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Carpal tunnel syndrome results from compression of which nerve?
questions.rationale: The median nerve passes through the carpal tunnel at the wrist and supplies the thumb, index and middle fingers.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Carpal tunnel syndrome (PDF p. 413)
questions.quote: It occurs when the median nerve at the wrist is compressed by thickened flexor sheath

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy waddles, falls often, and pushes on his thighs with his hands to stand up from the floor. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Gower's sign (using hands to climb up the legs) and pelvic girdle weakness are classic in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Muscular dystrophy (PDF p. 418)
questions.quote: Gower's sign (uses hands to push up from the floor.)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which laboratory result supports a diagnosis of Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
questions.rationale: Muscle damage raises serum enzymes, especially CK-MM; biopsy shows fibers replaced by fat.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Muscular dystrophy (PDF p. 418)
questions.quote: Serum enzymes are elevated, especially CK — MM.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 6-year-old has a limp and hip pain. X-ray shows aseptic necrosis of the femoral head. Which activity is best?
questions.rationale: In Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease, keep hip motion with low-impact activity such as swimming or cycling; avoid contact and high-impact sports.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease (PDF p. 416)
questions.quote: Encourage activities to maintain range of motion (swimming, bicycle riding).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which test is most commonly used to screen bone mineral density for osteoporosis?
questions.rationale: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) measures bone density; X-ray shows loss only when advanced.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Osteoporosis (PDF p. 417)
questions.quote: The most commonly used bone mineral density (BMD) screening is Dual — energ X — ray Absorptiometry (DXA).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should a client take alendronate (Fosamax)?
options: On rising, with water, staying upright
questions.rationale: Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water, stay upright 30 minutes, and wait 30 minutes before eating to prevent esophagitis and aid absorption.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Osteoporosis drugs (PDF p. 418)
questions.quote: The client should remain upright for 30 minutes after taking the medication.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An older woman has lost 5 cm of height and has a curved upper back. This posture is called:
questions.rationale: Vertebral collapse in osteoporosis causes loss of height and kyphosis (dowager's hump).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Osteoporosis (PDF p. 417)
questions.quote: Dowager's hump (curved upper back).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which advice helps a postmenopausal woman lower her osteoporosis risk?
questions.rationale: Regular weight-bearing exercise, calcium and vitamin D, and avoiding tobacco and alcohol protect bone mass.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Osteoporosis (PDF p. 417)
questions.quote: Exercise. At least 30 minutes, 5 days a week, then work up to 60 minutes.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A day after a below-knee amputation, the client says he feels his missing foot itching. The nurse explains:
options: He is confused and needs reorientation
He should ignore it; it is imagined
questions.rationale: Phantom limb sensation is expected and is discussed before surgery; phantom pain is treated with analgesics.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Amputation (PDF p. 414)
questions.quote: Phantom limb sensation as a normal occurrence

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Shortly after an amputation, a small bright red spot appears on the stump dressing. The nurse first:
options: Marks the spot to track bleeding
questions.rationale: Marking the edge of the drainage lets the nurse assess the rate of bleeding; a small spot early on is expected.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Amputation (PDF p. 414)
questions.quote: Observe stump dressing for signs of hemorrhage and mark outside of dressing so, rate of bleeding can be assessed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which stump care practice should the nurse teach a client with an amputation?
questions.rationale: Wash and dry the stump daily; wear cotton or wool socks; avoid lotions, powders, alcohol, nylon and torn socks.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Stump care (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: Wear cotton or woolen stump socks, avoid nylon socks.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Paget's disease of bone is caused by:
questions.rationale: Osteoclasts resorb bone rapidly and osteoblasts form excess abnormal bone that is weak and fractures easily.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Paget's disease (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: Increased rate of bone tissue breakdown (resorption) by osteoclasts followed by excessive abnormal bone formation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After a lumbar laminectomy, how should the client sit in a chair?
questions.rationale: A straight chair with feet flat prevents acute hip flexion, which may disrupt the operative site.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Laminectomy (PDF p. 412)
questions.quote: If patient is allowed to sit, use straight back chair and keep feet flat on floor.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which activity should a client avoid for several weeks after a laminectomy?
questions.rationale: Sweeping involves bending and stooping; walking without tiring is encouraged.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Critical thinking answers (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: after laminectomy, bending and stooping should be avoided. Sweeping involves bending and stooping.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client must wear a back brace after spinal fusion. Which skin care step is correct?
options: Wear a thin cotton shirt under it
Wear it directly on bare skin
questions.rationale: A thin cotton undershirt protects the skin; lotion and powder cake and irritate.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Critical thinking answers (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: Wearing a thin cotton undershirt under the brace protects the skin from the material of the brace.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After a spinal fusion with an iliac crest bone graft, the client reports pain at the hip. The nurse knows that:
options: It is a sign of fat embolism
It shows a spinal cord tear
questions.rationale: Clients may have considerable pain from the graft donor site; it takes about a year for the graft to become stable.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Spinal fusion (PDF p. 413)
questions.quote: Promote comfort — the client may have considerable pain from graft site.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before an MRI to check for a ruptured disc, the nurse should first ask about:
questions.rationale: The client lies in a tunnel-like scanner, so claustrophobia must be assessed (along with metal implants).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Critical thinking answers (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: In MRI, the client will be placed in a tunnel — like device. Therefore, it is important to assess for claustrophobia

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After arthroscopy of the knee, the nurse expects to:
options: Keep a pressure dressing for 24 hours
Keep the client NPO for 3 days
Start full sports the same day
questions.rationale: A pressure dressing for 24 hours prevents bleeding; activity is limited for several days.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Arthroscopy (PDF p. 394)
questions.quote: Pressure dressing over puncture site for 24 hours to prevent bleeding.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client in Russell traction should be checked often for pressure on the:
questions.rationale: Russell traction uses a sling under the knee; check the popliteal area for pressure sores and the leg for thrombophlebitis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Russell traction (PDF p. 398)
questions.quote: Assess back of the knee for pressure sores.; check the leg for signs and symptoms of thrombophlebitis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After open reduction and internal fixation of the hip, serosanguineous drainage collects in the wound drain. The nurse:
questions.rationale: Serosanguineous drainage is normal; empty the drain and record the amount, and report heavy bleeding or infection signs.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Open reduction care (PDF p. 401)
questions.quote: Empty hemovac. Serosanguinous drainage is normal.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client has widespread symmetrical tender points, poor sleep and fatigue, with normal joints. Which program helps most?
questions.rationale: Fibromyalgia is managed with graded aerobic exercise (at least 30 minutes, three times weekly), sleep care and medications.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Fibromyalgia (PDF p. 416)
questions.quote: regular aerobic exercises, a minimum of 30 minutes, three times weekly.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client using a continuous passive motion (CPM) machine after knee surgery needs the nurse to:
options: Keep the knee properly aligned on it
Stop it once pain is gone
Let the client set it freely
questions.rationale: Correct joint position on the CPM device ensures the ordered range of motion is done; settings change only as ordered.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Critical thinking answers (PDF p. 425)
questions.quote: Maintaining the knee joint on the CPM device ensures that ROM exercises are done.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which type of joint is the hip?
questions.rationale: Diarthroses are freely movable synovial joints such as the hip; the symphysis pubis is cartilaginous.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Anatomy (PDF p. 392)
questions.quote: Diarthrosis. Synovial joints; ball — and — socket joints (hips,

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before a bone scan, the nurse tells the client to:
questions.rationale: Voiding before the scan prevents bladder irritation by the radioisotope and gives clearer images; the client must stay still during the scan.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Bone scan (PDF p. 394)
questions.quote: Instruct client to void immedintcly before the procedure.
